court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court at Nagpur, Petition No.A-562/2013 and A-697/2013
case_name: Harish @ Roshan Bhaskar Karnewar vs Ms Leelavati @ Reena W/O Roshan Bhaskar

parties.respondent_defendant: Ms Leelavati @ Reena W/O Roshan Bhaskar, wife

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a petition for dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce. Respondent filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights. Trial court passed a common judgment dated 02/12/2016.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove that the other party has treated them with cruelty.
legal_principles.held: Replying to the contentions raised by the petitioner, learned Counsel for the respondent argues that the evidence of the Doctors led by the petitioner clearly brings on record that the respondent had suffered a seizure on a few occasions, but that the same has neither repeated nor is it a condition that she suffers continuously or that leaves her in a mental state as covered by the grounds under Section 13(1)(iii) of the Act.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not accept a party's version of events as true without sufficient evidence.
legal_principles.held: of the Court below that 'Epilepsy' was not a mental disorder or that the behaviour of the respondent constituting grounds of cruelty, had not been proved, were perverse and contrary to the weight of the evidence on record.

outcome.final_order: The final court order is not specified in the given excerpt.
